newsitem.title: USA: Georgia-Pacific profits down from year ago.
newsitem.headline: Georgia-Pacific profits down from year ago.

text.p: Georgia-Pacific Corp. Thursday reported a drop in third-quarter profits, saying pulp prices improved during the last three months but remain below levels earlier in the year.
It posted income of $99 million, or $1.09 a share, compared with an all-time record profit of $324 million, or $3.57 per share, in last year's third quarter.
"While pulp prices increased during the quarter, they have not returned to levels seen at the beginning of the year," said A.D. Correll, chairman and chief executive officer.
"Containerboard prices deteriorated during the quarter, and although prices for communication papers on average remained flat, we have seen some improvement in the last few weeks," he said.

"Building products performance was good during the summer months, improving slightly from the second quarter." he added. "Although lumber prices posted solid gains, structural panel prices, in particular oriented strand board, declined."
Georgia-Pacific's stock was off 25 cents at $78.25 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
